benchmark: big-ann-benchmarks NeurIPS'23 streaming track, msturing-30M-clustered, final_runbook.yaml (1,280 steps), mean recall@10 over 640 search checkpoints
status: measured on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) n2-custom-8-16384 VMs, not the organisers' Azure D8lds_v5 VM; not official and not a leaderboard result
warm_wheel: warm-python 0.6.8 (maturin --release --features python,experimental, built in the harness image)
comparison_commit: 0f81061b (previous pin of the same entry, same GCP host class, Docker mode): step-sum 3,563.1 s, run.py wall 3,566 s, one run, harness recall not exported

hardware.platform: GCP Compute Engine n2-custom-8-16384, us-east4 (r1b in us-east4-a, r2b in us-east4-b)
hardware.cpu: Intel Xeon @ 2.60 GHz, Ice Lake (Xeon 8370C class), 8 vCPU, AVX-512 with VBMI and VNNI

harness.fork: github.com/dcondrey/big-ann-benchmarks branch streaming/warm (PR harsha-simhadri/big-ann-benchmarks#357), commit 561f9fe plus a local config.yaml change to nprobe 925
harness.mode: Docker (image built from the entry's Dockerfile with WARM_COMMIT set to 5e2893f0, plus RUN pip3 install "numpy>=1.26,<2" as the last layer)
harness.command: python -u run.py --neurips23track streaming --algorithm warm --dataset msturing-30M-clustered --runbook_path neurips23/runbooks/final_runbook.yaml
harness.local_harness_changes: benchmark/runner.py: container memory limit forced to 8 GiB and wait timeout raised from 1 h to 3 h, for measurement only, so a run over the hour limit would be recorded instead of killed

algorithm_parameters: warm(partition_l5000_np925_ro1000, {'nprobe': 925}); build {mode partition, lists 5000, train_at 1000000, reorder 1000, T 8}
notes: Recall is the harness compute_metrics_all_runs k-nn mean over the exported HDF5 results, recomputed after the runs from the saved result files against the harness ground truth.
The two runs ran on two different VMs; their step sums differ by 54 s. They are two data points, not a guarantee, and the margin to 3,600 s on the slower run is 217 s.
The cgroup memory peak reads at the 8 GiB limit because it includes page cache; no OOM kill occurred in either run.
Timing on the organisers' Azure D8lds_v5 VM was not measured.
